title: Add reusable SLO query templates + label normalization (route/model/region/tier)
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes:
- Add versioned SLO query templates for rollout latency/error monitors
- Add label normalization helpers to map legacy labels -> canonical monitor identity fields
- Add unit tests and golden query snapshots for templates
body: Summary: This adds reusable, versioned SLO query templates and label normalization helpers to slo-toolkit so the rollout controller + monitor provisioning paths can consistently refer to the same monitor identity dimensions (route/model/region/tier). This is a prerequisite for wiring automated rollback to latency/error SLOs without chasing per-team label drift. Motivation / context: We’re standardizing monitor identities per ADR-0147 and need a single place to define (1) canonical label keys and (2) PromQL query templates that can be parameterized by route/model/region/customer tier. This PR is focused on the “toolkit” layer only (no controller code here) and is intended to be consumed by rollout-controller and the observability-pack dashboards/alerts. Linked work: ENG-2312 (controller consume monitors), ENG-2314 (evaluator semantics), ENG-2322 (label migration), INT-3310 (missing labels in some emitters). What’s included: 1) Canonical label set + normalization: - New module `pkg/identity/labels` defining canonical keys: `redwood_route`, `model_id`, `region`, `customer_tier`, plus optional `deployment_mode` and `workspace_id` for internal multi-tenant contexts. - New function `NormalizeLabels(in Labels) (Labels, Warnings)` that maps common legacy keys to canonical: `route`/`route_name` -> `redwood_route`, `model`/`model_name` -> `model_id`, `tier` -> `customer_tier`, `cloud_region` -> `region`. - Guardrails: strips empty values, trims whitespace, normalizes tier casing (e.g. `Dedicated` -> `dedicated`), and produces warnings when multiple legacy keys disagree. - Explicitly does NOT attempt to infer values from metric names; it only normalizes labels already present to avoid accidental cardinality blow-ups. 2) Query templates (versioned): - Added `pkg/templates/slo/v1` with templates for rollout decisioning: a) Latency (p95) query template (per route/model/region/tier): `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(redwood_llm_request_latency_bucket{redwood_route="{{route}}", model_id="{{model}}", region="{{region}}", customer_tier="{{tier}}"}[{{window}}])))` b) Error rate query template (5xx / total): `sum(rate(redwood_llm_requests_total{redwood_route="{{route}}", model_id="{{model}}", region="{{region}}", customer_tier="{{tier}}", status_code=~"5.."}[{{window}}])) / sum(rate(redwood_llm_requests_total{redwood_route="{{route}}", model_id="{{model}}", region="{{region}}", customer_tier="{{tier}}"}[{{window}}]))` - Added a small renderer that validates required params, escapes label values, and prevents users from injecting raw PromQL. - Added template metadata (template_id, version, required labels, metric dependencies) so downstream systems can log which query version they evaluated. 3) Docs: - `docs/rollouts/slo-query-templates.md` describing intended usage, required labels, and migration notes for legacy emitters. - Notes on exclusions: we do not include request warm-up filters in the PromQL; those remain in policy semantics (evaluator) to keep queries stable and dashboards aligned. Testing: - Unit tests for normalization edge cases (conflicting legacy labels, missing labels, whitespace/casing) and for escaping behavior. - “Golden” snapshots for rendered queries to catch accidental template changes; CI will fail if query output changes without updating the snapshot + changelog. - `go test ./...` and `golangci-lint` in CI. Implementation notes / decisions: - Tier is treated as a first-class label in templates because our SLO targets differ for hosted vs dedicated; this avoids ambiguous monitors and helps the controller bind the correct SLO per tenant mode. - We keep `model_id` as the canonical label name rather than `model` to reduce confusion with “model family” vs “version”; upstream emitters may still send `model`, and NormalizeLabels will map it. - Chose “v1” templates folder to make future changes explicit (e.g., adding exclusions, burn-rate helpers, or switching metrics). Backwards compatibility: - Existing consumers can keep using their own query strings; nothing is removed. - Normalization is additive; callers must opt in. - Added warnings but no hard errors unless required labels are missing at render time (callers can choose how strict to be). Files / areas changed (high level): - `pkg/identity/labels/canonical.go` - `pkg/identity/labels/normalize.go` - `pkg/templates/slo/v1/latency.go` - `pkg/templates/slo/v1/error_rate.go` - `pkg/templates/render/render.go` - `docs/rollouts/slo-query-templates.md` - `pkg/templates/slo/v1/testdata/*.golden` - Unit tests across `pkg/identity` and `pkg/templates` Commits (squashed): 1) `identity: add canonical labels + normalization warnings` 2) `templates: add v1 latency/error query templates + safe renderer` 3) `docs/tests: add template docs + golden snapshots` Review notes / conversation highlights: - Allison Grant: asked to align label names with ADR-0147 and ensure tier normalization is deterministic; requested adding explicit warnings on conflicting legacy inputs. Implemented: NormalizeLabels now emits `warning_conflicting_label_values` with the source keys. - Aisha Bello: requested that templates not encode policy semantics like “must be worse than baseline” or burn-rate windows; confirmed that evaluator will handle those. Added doc note clarifying that templates are intentionally “raw signal” queries and that alerting/evaluator choose windows. - Benji Okafor: requested a stable template_id/version string so rollout-controller can log what it used and avoid silent query drift; added `TemplateMeta{ID:"rollout_latency_p95", Version:"v1"}` and included it in render results. - Sergio Costa: requested label escaping and a lint check to prevent accidental regex injection; renderer now rejects values containing unescaped quotes and always renders equality matchers (no regex) for identity labels. CI: - build (ubuntu-latest): pass - go test: pass - golangci-lint: pass - snapshot-check: pass Merge: Squash merged by Nadia Rahman on 2025-02-21. Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Wire rollout-controller to use these templates when creating/looking up monitors (ENG-2312). - Backfill/migrate existing monitors/emitters to canonical labels (ENG-2322, INT-3310).
